facts: McKinsey surveyed a few hundred clients a few months before the talk
Top 20–25% of companies are seeing ~2x end-to-end improvement
An earlier survey at the end of the prior year showed meager gains
text: The top 20–25% of surveyed large enterprises are reporting 2x end-to-end improvements from AI in software development. Most companies still report modest 10–20% gains.

facts: Cycle length is one to two days instead of two-week sprints
Autonomous loops have expanded from build and test toward the product and release stages
text: Leading teams replace two-week Scrum sprints with Kanban-style one- to two-day loops in which agents run the 'night shift' and humans validate. Human review checkpoints are removed once confidence in a loop is established.

Teams are shrinking to pods of two to four people with collapsed roles. Product roles move toward a 'definer' role and dev/QA roles toward a 'builder' role. In the short term, halving pod size and doubling the team count while keeping the same planning math gives a quick acceleration 'cheat code'.

facts: ~1,700 skills were found for the single task of writing a PRD
text: Skill curation is now the hard part, not skill availability. One client found about 1,700 downloadable skills just for writing a PRD. Organizations should curate a handful that fit their context.

Quality is dropping even per developer and per PR as code generation speeds up. The recommended fix is to feed agents curated 'golden examples' rather than the average of the codebase, and to encode standards at every PDLC checkpoint instead of relying on end-of-pipeline quality gates.

facts: Example: a bank's customer-facing app had color-scheme and colorblind accessibility rules
text: As build and test compress, the bottleneck shifts upstream to requirements, downstream to release, and 'sideways' to parallel teams such as risk, compliance and design. One bank's color-scheme and colorblind-accessibility rules had to be encoded into the agents.
Measuring impact remains the least mature area. Some clients are experimenting with using AI to score the value and intent of work so they can direct tokens and resources to the highest-value items.
